subject: RFP: Commercial & invoicing model — consumption smoothing and invoice credits
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medtechco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedTechCo Procurement <procurement@medtechco.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: RFP commercial section — invoice smoothing & credits

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the draft RFP response — we're reviewing the commercial section now. A couple of quick clarifying items from procurement that will determine which pricing path we recommend internally:

1) "Consumption smoothing" — can you confirm if Redwood applies any invoice-level credit when actual monthly consumption is under the committed band (i.e., do unused committed tokens convert to credits on next invoice)?
2) "Overage reconciliation" — proposed cadence for true-ups (monthly? quarterly?), and whether overages are billed at a flat rate or tiered.
3) Billing visibility — procurement would like a sample invoice layout that separates committed consumption, burst/overage charges, and any credits.

We're trying to compare apples-to-apples vs. two other vendors; these three points would help. Also, please confirm if any promotional overage rate can be applied during an introductory period.

If easier, we can set a short 30-min call this week.

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Procurement
MedTechCo
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medtechco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP commercial section — invoice smoothing & credits

Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Attached is a short commercial summary and a sample invoice layout that shows how we present committed vs overage vs credits. High level answers below; happy to hop on a call to walk through calculations.

Summary (commercial option we normally propose for enterprise RFPs):
- Commit structure: monthly committed token band (example: 500M tokens/month) at an agreed unit price. Commit priced with a 20% discount to our public list rate in the example attachment.
- Consumption smoothing / credits: any unused committed token value converts to an "invoice credit" that applies to subsequent invoices for up to 6 months. Credits are monetary (USD) not token buckets, so they show as a credit line on the invoice and reduce the net amount due. Credits can roll forward for 6 months; beyond that they expire.
- True-up cadence: monthly true-up with a 60-day reconciliation window. We issue the provisional invoice at month-end, then finalise after a 60-day audit window to allow for reconciliations and usage attribution.
- Overage billing: tiered overage rates that step down as consumption grows within a month (e.g., Tier 1: up to +20% at base overage rate; Tier 2: +20–50% at discounted overage rate; Tier 3: >50% at further discounted rate). Attachment includes a worked example showing effective blended rate at different utilization curves.
- Introductory promotion: for the first 6 months we can offer a 15% promotional reduction on overage rates to give you buffer while you stabilize traffic patterns.
- Reserved / dedicated option: for predictable, high-throughput workloads, Dedicated nodes can be contracted with a flat committed spend (monthly license) and separate per-token run usage; we can model this in the attached spreadsheet.

Next steps: if this aligns, I'll prepare a short commercial term sheet and DocuSign for an LOI. If you want alternate credit rules (e.g., token roll vs monetary credit) we can draft that as a negotiated term.

Attachments: Redwood_MedTech_Commercial_Summary_v2.pdf (commercial summary + worked examples), MedTech_Sample_Invoice_Layout.xlsx

Thanks,
Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: MedTechCo RFP — pricing guardrails and margin checks

Hannah / Ben — quick internal note that I'd like us to protect margin on the promotional overage and the 6-month rolling credit. Suggested guardrails:
- Cap credit exposure to 20% of committed monthly ARR per rolling 6-month window (prevents large carry-forwards on underconsumption).
- Make promotional overage reduction apply to first 6 months only and only to first two overage tiers; higher tiers should revert to standard overage pricing.
- Include an SLA-backed latency clause only in Dedicated/DPA options — don't add high-cost SLAs on hosted commits without a clear uplift.

If we get pushback from procurement, offer a three-month pilot with measured telemetry and an operational acceptance criteria (ops runbook + usage expectations) before full 12-month commit.

Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medtechco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedTechCo Procurement <procurement@medtechco.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP commercial section — invoice smoothing & credits

Hannah — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from procurement after reviewing the sample invoice:

- Confirming: credits are monetary and not token buckets (good). Can credits be applied to future invoices automatically, or do we need to raise a credit note? We prefer automatic application.
- Credit expiry: 6 months is acceptable, but procurement asks for a dashboard export we can run to reconcile before expiry.
- Regional pricing: can you confirm whether the committed unit price in the example applies to US-only usage? We have EU traffic too and need a regional breakout in the final term sheet (EUR conversions and VAT handling).

Procurement is also asking if Redwood can cap month-over-month invoice volatility for the first two quarters (e.g., limit month-to-month increase above committed to a preset percent) — they understand this is contractual and can be a capped overage multiplier. Is that something Redwood would entertain on a trial basis?

If you can confirm the above and send the invoice export sample, we can advance to commercial marking and internal legal review.

Best,
Elena
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medtechco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: RFP commercial section — invoice smoothing & credits

Elena — appreciate the detailed questions. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) Credits application: credits are applied automatically to subsequent invoices. We include a credit line on the next provisional invoice; clients can see the remaining credit balance on the Redwood Console and export a reconciliation report (CSV) — attached is a sample invoice and a screenshot of the export fields.

2) Credit expiry & reconciliation: credits roll forward for 6 months and expire after that. We'll provide a monthly "Credit Balance" export that shows issued credits, consumed credits, and expiry date for each credit line so your procurement team can reconcile before expiry.

3) Regional pricing: the example in the commercial summary is US pricing. We will produce a two-line split in the final term sheet (US tokens vs EU tokens) and include EUR conversions with net-of-VAT handling. For the RFP response, I'll include a short footnote specifying region-specific uplift for EU due to additional infra and data transfer costs.

4) Invoice volatility cap (trial): Redwood can offer a capped month-over-month invoice increase for Q1–Q2 of the contract as a trial: cap at +40% over committed invoice amount (after credits) per month. This would be a contractual term limited to the first 6 months of the committed period. We'll model the impact in the term sheet — note this reduces our ability to credit large underconsumptions, so we'll pair it with the 20% cap on credit exposure Karthik recommended.

5) Pilot option: if you'd like low-friction validation, propose a 3-month pilot at 50% of the committed band with promotional overage rates; afterwards we can convert to full commit with a pro-rated true-up. This eases the procurement/finance sign-off.

I've attached: MedTech_Sample_Invoice_Layout.xlsx and an updated commercial summary (Redwood_MedTech_Commercial_Summary_v2.pdf). I'll prepare a short commercial term sheet that incorporates: (a) monthly commit band, (b) 6-month credit roll, (c) 60-day finalisation window, (d) tiered overage with 15% promo on overages for first 6 months, (e) invoice volatility cap for Q1–Q2 at +40%.

Would you be available Wed 1 Sep 10am PT for a 30-min align call? If so I'll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign LOI to lock the pricing while legal finalises the contract.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.
Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
